label: prop:binding-alpha-shift-extension
title: Binding A≥3 via per-rep Reeb phase at a force-carrier torus knot
html:
The light-atom binding energy B(A) = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T(p_A, k_A)) is uniquely determined by (i) the substrate-universal per-rep Reeb coupling \rho_0 pinned by the deuteron, and (ii) the substrate-fixed force-carrier torus knot T(p_A, k_A) per nucleus. Both legs route through the proved \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = k\cdot(p-1) formula (prop:alpha-shift-torus-knot). The binding closure is

  B(A) = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T(p_A, k_A))
       = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot k_A \cdot (p_A - 1).

The candidate (p, k) values per nucleus are hypothesised; the rigorous identification from the substrate's Hecke-Wedderburn block structure on H_{3A}(q) is open.

The A \ge 3 binding gap, the per-nucleus candidate table and its rationale, the Lean structure, and the remaining open math are collected in the binding-extension derivation context.

Status (owner ruling, 2026-09-05): retired as a knot-selection route. Its atom-to-knot assignments are chosen from a census so the knot's volume reproduces B_AME/m_e — the A ∈ {5,6,7} gap exists precisely because no census knot has the right volume — and the ^4He "magic" rule is 4\times the ^3He prediction using the same \mathrm{Vol}(L6a4) = 8G, so it is not an independent confirmation. Kept for the record, not as a live binding route. See docs/audits/2026-09-05-binding-route-consolidation-no-knot-selection.md.
